title: Minimal Polynomial vs Characteristic Polynomial of Matrices
description: Formalizes the fundamental relationship between minimal and characteristic polynomials of matrices: minpoly K M divides charpoly M, both are monic, minpoly annihilates M (Cayley-Hamilton variant), and roots of minpoly are roots of charpoly. 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The characteristic polynomial det(λI − M) was central to Cauchy's eigenvalue work (1829) and formalized by Weierstrass (1858) in the context of bilinear forms. The Cayley-Hamilton theorem — every matrix satisfies its own characteristic polynomial — was announced by Cayley for 2×2 and 3×3 cases in 1858 and by Hamilton for quaternions the same year; the full n×n proof was given by Frobenius (1878) using invariant factors and the rational canonical form. The minimal polynomial emerged from Frobenius's invariant factor theory: m_M is the largest invariant factor of (λI − M), equivalently the GCD of all (n−1)×(n−1) minors of (λI − M) divided by the GCD of all entries. The fundamental theorem minpoly | charpoly follows from Cayley-Hamilton (charpoly annihilates M) and the universal property of minpoly (it divides any annihilating polynomial). The minimal polynomial governs the primary decomposition of K^n as a K[X]-module and determines the Jordan structure: M is diagonalizable over K iff minpoly has no repeated roots; M has a cyclic vector iff minpoly = charpoly. This file provides the foundational infrastructure for Jordan normal form theory in Lean 4.
overview.problemStatement: Prove: (1) minpoly K M divides charpoly M. (2) Both are monic. (3) charpoly annihilates M (Cayley-Hamilton). (4) minpoly degree ≤ dim(M). (5) Roots of minpoly are roots of charpoly.
overview.proofStrategy: Most results follow from Mathlib's minpoly and charpoly APIs. minpoly_dvd_charpoly: use minpoly.dvd and charpoly_monic. charpoly_annihilates: Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly. minpoly_annihilates: minpoly.aeval.
keyInsights: **Divisibility**: minpoly(M) | charpoly(M) because charpoly(M)[M] = 0 (Cayley-Hamilton) and minpoly(M) divides any annihilating polynomial.
**Degree bounds**: deg(minpoly) ≤ n = dim(K^n) since the n+1 matrices {I, M, M², ..., M^n} are linearly dependent in Mat_n(K).
**Root relationship**: Every root of minpoly is a root of charpoly (divisibility). The converse may fail (Jordan blocks).
**Cayley-Hamilton**: charpoly(M)(M) = 0 — the matrix satisfies its own characteristic polynomial.

**Universal property generates the annihilator ideal**: minpoly generates Ann(M) = {p ∈ K[X] | p(M) = 0} as a principal ideal. Equivalently, p(M) = 0 iff minpoly | p. This makes minpoly the unique 'canonical' annihilating polynomial from which all others derive.

sections.title: Module Header, Imports, and Setup
sections.summary: Module docstring stating what is proved (relationships between the minimal and characteristic polynomials of a matrix), key results, mathematical context, status, and Mathlib dependencies; opens the MinpolyCharpoly namespace with Matrix/Polynomial scopes and the matrix index variables.
sections.mathContext: Sets up the study of $m_M = \mathrm{minpoly}_K M$ and $p_M = M.\mathrm{charpoly}$ for an $n \times n$ matrix $M$ over a field $K$, with $n$ a `Fintype` with `DecidableEq`.

sections.title: Part 1: Core Relationship
sections.summary: Establishes that every matrix is integral over its base ring (matrix_is_integral) and the core divisibility minpoly_dvd_charpoly: the minimal polynomial divides the characteristic polynomial.
sections.mathContext: $M$ is integral over $K$, so $m_M$ is defined, and $m_M \mid p_M$ in $K[X]$ — the fundamental relationship between the two polynomials.

sections.title: Part 2: Properties of the Minimal Polynomial
sections.summary: Records that the minimal polynomial is monic (minpoly_monic) and has positive degree for a nontrivial matrix ring (minpoly_degree_pos).
sections.mathContext: $m_M$ is monic and $\deg(m_M) \ge 1$ whenever $\mathrm{Matrix}\,n\,n\,K$ is nontrivial.

sections.title: Part 3: Degree Bounds
sections.summary: Bounds the minimal polynomial degree: minpoly_degree_le_charpoly_degree (≤ deg charpoly via natDegree_le_of_dvd) and minpoly_degree_le_dim (≤ n via charpoly_natDegree_eq_dim).
sections.mathContext: $1 \le \deg(m_M) \le \deg(p_M) = n$, where $n = \mathrm{Fintype.card}\,n$, using that $p_M$ is monic hence nonzero.

sections.title: Part 4: Annihilation Properties
sections.summary: Both polynomials annihilate the matrix: charpoly_annihilates (Cayley-Hamilton, from Mathlib) and minpoly_annihilates (defining property), plus the universal property minpoly_divides_annihilator that minpoly divides any annihilating polynomial.
sections.mathContext: $p_M(M) = 0$ (Cayley–Hamilton) and $m_M(M) = 0$; moreover $p(M) = 0 \Leftrightarrow m_M \mid p$, so the annihilator ideal is $(m_M)$.

sections.title: Part 5: Both Polynomials are Monic
sections.summary: Proves both_monic: the minimal and characteristic polynomials are each monic.
sections.mathContext: Both $m_M$ and $p_M$ are monic, a prerequisite for the degree and divisibility arguments.

sections.title: Part 6: Root Relationship
sections.summary: Proves minpoly_root_is_charpoly_root: every root of the minimal polynomial is also a root of the characteristic polynomial (the two share their root set / eigenvalues).
sections.mathContext: If $\alpha$ is a root of $m_M$ then $\alpha$ is a root of $p_M$, since $m_M \mid p_M$; the roots are exactly the eigenvalues of $M$.

sections.title: Part 7: The Linear Map Connection
sections.summary: Proves minpoly_eq_linmap_minpoly: the minimal polynomial of a matrix equals that of its associated linear map (via Matrix.minpoly_toLin'), establishing basis-independence.
sections.mathContext: $m_M = m_\phi$ where $\phi$ is the endomorphism represented by $M$, so the minimal polynomial is independent of the chosen basis.

sections.title: Part 8: Concrete Examples
sections.summary: Works the extremal examples: the identity matrix (minpoly = X − 1) and the zero matrix (minpoly = X), with their annihilation and divisibility checks — the cases of maximal degree gap n − 1.
sections.mathContext: Identity: $m_I = X-1$, $p_I = (X-1)^n$. Zero: $m_0 = X$, $p_0 = X^n$. Both realize the maximal degree gap $\deg(p) - \deg(m) = n-1$.

sections.title: Part 9: Uniqueness of Minimal Polynomial
sections.summary: Proves minpoly_dvd_annihilating_monic: the minimal polynomial divides any monic annihilating polynomial — the universal property uniquely characterizing it.
sections.mathContext: For any monic $p$ with $p(M) = 0$, $m_M \mid p$; together with monicity this determines $m_M$ uniquely.

sections.title: Summary of Results
sections.summary: Closing documentation block grouping all 17 results by theme — divisibility, degree bounds, annihilation, structure, and the linear-map connection — giving the complete picture of the minpoly/charpoly relationship.
sections.mathContext: Synthesizes the file: $m_M \mid p_M$, $\deg(m_M) \le n$, both annihilate $M$ and are monic, share roots, and the matrix minpoly agrees with the linear-map minpoly.

conclusion.summary: Minpoly-charpoly relationship fully formalized: 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Divisibility, annihilation, degree bounds, and root relationships all proved.
conclusion.implications: This provides the core infrastructure for Jordan normal form theory in Lean 4. The minpoly | charpoly relationship is fundamental to understanding diagonalizability (minpoly splits into distinct linear factors) vs. Jordan decomposition.
openQuestions: Can the Jordan normal form theorem be formalized in Lean 4 using this infrastructure?
Can the characterization of diagonalizable matrices (minpoly has no repeated roots) be proved?
Can the rational canonical form (based on minpoly factorization) be formalized?

crossReferences.description: Cayley-Hamilton (charpoly(M)(M) = 0) is the key ingredient: it makes charpoly an annihilating polynomial, from which minpoly | charpoly follows via the universal property
Companion entry formalizing minpoly reduction (any f(M) = f mod minpoly, evaluated at M) and the annihilator ideal Ann(M) = (minpoly) in K[X]
Cyclic vector theory: M has a cyclic vector iff minpoly(M) = charpoly(M), the case of minimum degree gap — complementary to the extremal examples (I, 0) where the gap is maximal
Polynomial reduction via minpoly: for any polynomial f, aeval M f = aeval M (f mod minpoly), leveraging the universal property proved here
